The original Metal Gear Solid, actually the third game in the series, was first conceived as a 3DO game in 1994. The 3DO, which was first released in late 1993, is considered by many to be the first console of the fifth generation, complete with 3D graphics and games on CD-ROM. However, competition from older consoles and new ones like the Saturn and PlayStation meant it died within a couple of years. It had similar specifications as the original PlayStation, which likely contributed to it being made for that platform rather than the Saturn, which had more of an emphasis on 2D graphics, or the N64, as cartridges couldn't contain the amount of cutscenes and voice acting Hideo Kojima wanted.

The reason why Metal Gear Solid was not simply called Metal Gear 3 was because even Kojima thought the first two games were obscure. Solid was a reference to how the polygonal graphic appeared compared to sprites.

Metal Gear Solid eventually sold over six million copies worldwide, making it the tenth best-selling game on the PlayStation. It is often regarded as the beginning of a Konami's being a major player in console gaming. Prior to it, Konami's only notable major hit in years was Castlevania: Symphony of the Night in 1997. Over the following decade, Konami would release three numbered Metal Gear Solid sequels, the Pro Evolution Soccer series, Dance Dane Revolution, Yu-Gi-Oh titles, the Silent Hill series, and various other games.
